question.problem:
The temperature of a metal rod, measured in degrees Celsius, is given by the function $T(t)$, where $t$ is the time, in hours, since the heating began. The values of $T(t)$ for different values of $t$ are given in the table below:

| $t$ | $3$ | $6$ | $9$ | $12$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $T(t)$ | $18$ | $21$ | $27$ | $30$ |

Approximate the rate of change of the temperature when $t=12$ using a backward difference approximation. Do not round the answer.

The estimated rate of change when $t=12$ is
{{field-1}} degrees Celsius per hour.
question.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{T}^{′}(t)≈\frac{T(t)-T(t-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the time $t=12.$ We choose the step size $h$ to be as small as possible, in this case $h=3.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(12) & ≈\frac{T(12)-T(12-3)}{3} \\  & =\frac{T(12)-T(9)}{3} \\  & =\frac{30-27}{3} \\  & =\frac{3}{3} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the estimated rate of change when $t=12$ is $1$ degrees Celsius per hour.
